advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the canary `advisory-alert`/close path against an audit step that did not complete (e.g. gate on the audit step's success/outcome or emit `blocking` even on infra failure) so a DB outage cannot auto-close a live advisory ticket.
evidence: dependency-advisory-canary.yml audit step: `continue-on-error: true` then `python scripts/dependency_audit.py gate --lane branch`
advisory-alert step guarded only by `if: env.DRY_RUN == 'false'` with `BLOCKING: ${{ steps.audit.outputs.blocking }}`

scripts/dependency_audit.py cmd_gate: on `run_pip_audit` error it prints the INFRASTRUCTURE message and `return 1` BEFORE the `gh_output = environ.get("GITHUB_OUTPUT")` write block, so `blocking` output is never set
cmd_advisory_alert: `blocking = environ.get("BLOCKING", "false") == "true"` then `elif not blocking and tid:` runs the `rebar transition ... open closed` close path
Fail-run step `if: steps.audit.outputs.blocking == 'true'` is also false when the output is empty, so the infra failure is not surfaced as red either
advisory.finding: The canary's `advisory-alert` step runs on any non-DRY_RUN outcome and reads `BLOCKING` from `steps.audit.outputs.blocking`, but `cmd_gate` returns 1 WITHOUT writing GITHUB_OUTPUT when `run_pip_audit` fails (DB unreachable / unparseable JSON). With `continue-on-error: true` on the audit step, an infra failure leaves `blocking` empty, so `advisory-alert` treats it as non-blocking and, if an advisory ticket already exists, CLOSES it — auto-closing a live advisory ticket on a transient advisory-DB outage.
scenarios: Daily canary run where OSV/PyPI is unreachable while an advisory ticket is open
advisory.suggested_fix: Have cmd_gate write GITHUB_OUTPUT (or a distinct `audit_ok=false`) even on infra failure, and gate the canary's advisory-alert close branch on the audit having actually run — e.g. `if: steps.audit.outcome != 'skipped'` plus requiring a non-empty `blocking`/`audit_ok` before taking the close branch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Before auto-closing, confirm the ticket was canary-filed (e.g. match `--detected-by dependency-advisory-canary` or the advisory marker) rather than closing any open bug with the tag.
evidence: scripts/alert_dedup.py find_alert_ticket queries only `--type=bug --status=open --has-tag={tag}` and returns `tickets[0]["ticket_id"]`

scripts/dependency_audit.py cmd_advisory_alert close branch `elif not blocking and tid:` transitions that ticket open->closed with no check that the canary itself filed it (no detected-by/marker verification)
advisory.finding: The advisory-clear close path closes whatever OPEN bug carries the advisory tag, since `find_alert_ticket` matches by tag only. A human-filed bug tagged `dependency-advisory-alert` would be auto-closed by the canary the first time the audit is non-blocking.
scenarios: An engineer manually opens a bug with the dependency-advisory-alert tag; the next clean canary run closes it

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep in test_failure_output_points_at_the_runbook with an assertion on emitted output (e.g. runbook path present in stdout/stderr of a blocking gate run through main()).
evidence: tests/unit/test_dependency_advisory_wiring.py:160-161: `module = (_ROOT / "scripts" / "dependency_audit.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"); assert "docs/dependency-advisory-runbook.md" in module`
Contrast the behavioral form already used at tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py:266 `assert mod.RUNBOOK in captured.out` and :282 `assert mod.RUNBOOK_URL in capsys.readouterr().err`
advisory.finding: test_failure_output_points_at_the_runbook reads scripts/dependency_audit.py's SOURCE TEXT and asserts the literal string 'docs/dependency-advisory-runbook.md' is present, rather than asserting the runbook path is EMITTED at runtime. This is source-grepping of the code under test: it verifies the implementation text, not observable behavior, and is a change-detector (it breaks if the path is assembled from RUNBOOK/RUNBOOK_URL constants differently while still being printed correctly, and passes even if no failure path actually prints it). It is redundant with the behavioral assertion already present (test_gate_gerrit_exit_zero_for_an_unrelated_change asserts `mod.RUNBOOK in captured.out`).
scenarios: A refactor that builds the runbook link from RUNBOOK/RUNBOOK_URL constants keeps the emitted output identical but could trip/skew this text grep
The grep passes even if a failure path stopped printing the runbook, giving false assurance
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the read_text grep; assert `mod.RUNBOOK in captured.out` (or `.err`) from a `mod.main(["gate", ...])` invocation that produces a blocking or advisory verdict — the behavior the test claims to protect.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an osv_severity/collect_findings test using a realistic OSV payload shape (CVSS-vector severity and/or top-level `severity` list) to pin how enrichment classifies it.
evidence: scripts/dependency_audit.py osv_severity reads `specific.get("severity")` and only accepts a plain str; the tests feed only word severities: gate_runner builds `json.dumps({"database_specific": {"severity": severity}})` with severity in {HIGH, MEDIUM, CRITICAL} (tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py:87)
test_osv_enrichment_downgrades_a_medium (line 166) and test_unrated_advisory_is_treated_as_high (line 156) are the only enrichment-shape tests; both use bare-word severities
ABSENCE: no test with a CVSS-vector severity string or an OSV top-level `severity` list, which are the shapes OSV actually returns
advisory.finding: osv_severity() returns whatever string OSV places in database_specific.severity, uppercased, and classify() maps any non-MEDIUM/MODERATE/LOW value (including a CVSS vector string like 'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/...') to 'fail'. Real OSV payloads commonly express severity as a CVSS vector or as a top-level list, not the bare words 'CRITICAL'/'HIGH'/'MEDIUM'/'LOW' the tests use. No test exercises a realistic OSV severity payload shape, so a regression in the enrichment/parse path (e.g. mis-handling a CVSS vector, or the top-level `severity` array OSV also emits) would not be caught — enrichment could silently degrade to the HIGH fallback (stricter) or, if the parse changed, mis-rate a real MEDIUM as fail without detection.
scenarios: OSV returns severity as a CVSS vector in database_specific.severity
OSV returns severity only in the top-level `severity` array

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin pip-audit to a specific version (and ideally hash) across all three workflow lanes.
evidence: "uv pip install pip-audit" appears in _build-and-test.yml, dependency-advisory-canary.yml, and release.yml
comment: "pip-audit is a scan TOOL, not a dependency of the project — kept out of the lock."
scripts/dependency_audit.py parse_pip_audit_json depends on pip-audit's JSON shape ({dependencies:[{vulns:[...]}]}), which a new pip-audit version could change
advisory.finding: pip-audit is installed unpinned (`uv pip install pip-audit`) in all three lanes; because pip-audit's version determines the gate's behavior and output format (parsed by scripts/dependency_audit.py), an upstream pip-audit release could silently change results or break parsing, and there is no version/hash pin or lock entry for it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Install a pinned version, e.g. `uv pip install 'pip-audit==<version>'`, kept in sync across _build-and-test.yml, dependency-advisory-canary.yml, and release.yml.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin actions/checkout and actions/setup-python to full commit SHAs (with version comments) to match the setup-uv pinning posture.
evidence: "uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9  # v9.0.0" (SHA-pinned)
"uses: actions/checkout@v7" (tag-pinned)
"uses: actions/setup-python@v7" (tag-pinned)
advisory.finding: Action pinning posture is inconsistent: setup-uv is pinned to a full commit SHA (with version comment), but actions/checkout and actions/setup-python are pinned only to floating major tags (@v7), which can be moved by the upstream owner and undermines the SHA-pin provenance guarantee.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a bounded timeout to the OSV curl call and document/pin the OSV enrichment dependency (endpoint + tool) as an intentional external provenance source.
evidence: runner(["curl", "-fsS", f"https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/{vuln_id}"])
RUNBOOK states severity is enriched from OSV (database_specific.severity) at scan time
no --max-time / connect timeout on the curl invocation
advisory.finding: scripts/dependency_audit.py introduces a new runtime dependency on an external provenance service (api.osv.dev) invoked via `curl` subprocess with no timeout; the severity classification (and thus the gate verdict) now depends on an external HTTP endpoint reached with an unpinned, ambient `curl` binary.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `--max-time`/`--connect-timeout` to the curl argv (e.g. `["curl", "-fsS", "--max-time", "10", url]`).
